mappings.note: Content matches: Ananias, elders, Tertullus appearing before the governor against Paul.

Translation v2 ends at 'commença à l'accuser, en disant :'. The actual speech content begins in Translation v3. OSMAIN v2 includes the start of the speech ('Da Paulus var ført fram...'). This is a split of the narrative flow.

Translation v3 contains the beginning of Tertullus's speech ('Très-excellent Félix...'). OSMAIN v2 contains this same text. The split between v2 and v3 in the translation separates the narrative intro from the speech content.
Content matches: Request to not take too much time and to listen briefly.
Content matches: Accusation of being a pest/seditionist among Jews and leader of Nazarenes.

Translation v6 includes 'et l'avons voulu juger selon notre Loi' (and we wanted to judge him according to our Law). OSMAIN v6 only says: 'Han forsøkte også å vanhellige tempelet, og derfor grep vi ham.' The OSMAIN text lacks the specific detail about wanting to judge him by their law.
Content matches: Lysias taking Paul away with great power and ordering accusers to come to the governor.
Content matches: Invitation for the governor to question Paul himself.
Content matches: Jews supporting the accusation and claiming it is true.
Content matches: Paul responding after being signaled by the governor, acknowledging Felix's years as judge.
Content matches: Not more than twelve days since going to Jerusalem to worship.
Content matches: Not found disputing or inciting crowds in temple, synagogues, or city.
Content matches: Accusers cannot prove their charges.
Content matches: Confession of serving God according to 'the Way', believing Law and Prophets.
Content matches: Hope in resurrection of just and unjust.
Content matches: Striving to have a clear conscience before God and men.
Content matches: Coming after several years to bring gifts/offering.
Content matches: Found in temple ritually cleansed, without crowd or uproar.

Translation v20 is split. Translation v19 ends at 'd'Asie,' (of Asia). OSMAIN v19 contains the full sentence: 'Men noen jøder fra Asia-provinsen burde ha vært her foran deg og fremmet sin anklage, om de hadde noe imot meg.' The translation splits this into two verses.
Translation v20 continues the sentence from v19: 'Qui devaient comparaître devant toi...'. This completes OSMAIN v19.

Translation v21 starts with 'Ou que ceux-ci eux-mêmes disent...' which corresponds to the second half of OSMAIN v20 ('Eller la disse som er her...'). The first part of OSMAIN v20 is in Translation v20? No, looking closely: OSMAIN v20 is one sentence. Translation splits it. Wait, let's re-evaluate 19/20/21 mapping.
Content matches: The specific cry about resurrection of the dead being the only charge.

Translation v23 ends abruptly with 'entièreme' (incomplete word). It covers the first part of OSMAIN v22 ('Men Feliks... utsatte saken og sa: ...'). The second half of OSMAIN v22 is missing or cut off in this translation verse.
Content matches: Order to guard Paul with leniency and allow friends to help.

Translation v25 covers the first half of OSMAIN v24 ('Noen dager senere... hørte ham tale om troen på Kristus Jesus'). The second half of OSMAIN v24 is missing? No, looking at Translation v26. Wait, let's check the flow.
Content matches: Paul speaking of righteousness, self-control, judgment; Felix frightened and saying 'Go now'.
Content matches: Felix hoping for money, sending for Paul often to talk.
Content matches: Two years later, Festus succeeds Felix; Felix leaves Paul in prison to please Jews.

extraContent.description: Translation includes 'et l'avons voulu juger selon notre Loi' (and we wanted to judge him according to our Law). OSMAIN v6 does not contain this phrase.
